title: Dinner with your partner’s family
setting: Your partner Dewi has brought you to meet her parents for the first time, at their home in Bandung. You arrive late in the afternoon, and both of them come to the door.

n1.speaker: mother
n1.indonesian: Eh, sudah sampai. Ayo, masuk, masuk.
n1.english: Oh, you're here. Come in, come in.

options.feedback: Just right: a time-of-day greeting, with Om and Tante for her parents. If Dewi touches their hands to her forehead (salim), do the same.
Permisi as you step into someone's home is polite and natural. Slip your shoes off at the door if theirs are there.
Kamu to your partner's mother sounds like talking down to her. Use her title in place of 'you': Apa kabar, Tante?

n2.speaker: father
n2.indonesian: Oh, ini Sam, ya? Dewi sudah banyak cerita.
n2.english: So you're Sam. Dewi's told us a lot about you.

options.feedback: Confirms it, and says how you know Dewi. Agree with her beforehand how you'll be introduced: some families prefer teman (friend) at first.
Thanking them for having you is right at any point, and worth saying again as you leave.
Correct, but Anda sounds like a business meeting. With family, use his title: Senang bisa bertemu dengan Om.

n3.speaker: mother
n3.indonesian: Ayo, kita makan dulu. Tante masak dari pagi, lho.
n3.english: Come on, let's eat. I've been cooking since this morning, you know.

options.feedback: What you say when a host has gone to trouble. It isn't a refusal: she'll serve you anyway, and you accept with thanks.
Praise before the first bite: any cook likes to hear it. Notice she called herself Tante: elders often use their own title for 'I'.

options.indonesian: Tidak usah, Tante. Saya belum lapar.
options.english: There's no need. I'm not hungry yet.
options.feedback: Turning down a meal she's spent the day cooking would hurt. Say jangan repot-repot if you like, then sit down and eat.

n4.speaker: mother
n4.english: Go on, have some more. Don't be shy.

options.feedback: Thanks, sudah (that's enough) and a reason nobody can argue with. Expect to be urged again, and say it again warmly.
Taking a little more pleases the cook, and is often kinder than refusing a second time.
Tidak mau is how a child refuses. Give thanks and a reason: Sudah, Tante, terima kasih. Saya sudah kenyang.

n5.speaker: father
n5.english: So what do you do here, Sam?

options.indonesian: Saya mengajar bahasa Inggris, Om. Sudah dua tahun di sini.
options.english: I teach English. I've been here two years.
options.feedback: A full, friendly answer with Om. He said Sam rather than 'you': Indonesians often use your name in its place.
Grammatical, but adalah makes it sound like a written definition. Indonesian needs no 'am': Saya guru bahasa Inggris, Om.
A one-word answer sounds curt to an elder. Add Om, and a little more: where you teach, or for how long.
The classic answer: warm, and it promises nothing. A smile does the rest.
Flat, and it can sound as if you're not serious about Dewi. Keep it light: Doakan saja, ya, Tante.
Polite words, but it shuts her out. Kapan nikah? is friendly interest at every family gathering, and it wants a light answer, not a wall.

n7.speaker: father
n7.indonesian: Lho, kok buru-buru? Baru jam delapan.
n7.english: Oh, what's the hurry? It's only eight.

options.feedback: Pamit is taking your leave properly. Say it to each of them, and thank them again for the meal.

options.indonesian: Sudah malam, Om. Besok saya kerja pagi. Terima kasih banyak, ya, Om, Tante.
options.english: It's getting late, and I'm working early tomorrow. Thank you so much.
options.feedback: A reason makes leaving gentle, and the thanks goes to both of them.
Bye-bye is for friends and children. With a partner's parents, take your leave with pamit: Saya pamit dulu, Om, Tante.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Done. Om and Tante (or Bapak and Ibu) in place of 'you', jangan repot-repot when the food appears, sudah kenyang with thanks when it keeps coming, a light Doakan saja for the wedding question, and pamit to each of the elders as you leave: a good first impression.
